newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LEICESTER CITY LEAGUE CUP FINAL SQUAD PENPIX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEICESTER CITY LEAGUE CUP FINAL SQUAD PENPIX.

text.p: LONDON, April 4 (reuter) - Pen pictures of the Leicester City players likely to comprise the squad for the League Cup final against Middlesbrough at Wembley on Sunday:

Kasey Keller, goalkeeper, 28. Keller has been in outstanding form this season following his 800,000 pounds ($1.3 million) move from Millwall in the close season. An American international regular, Keller has helped Leicester establish themselves in the premier league.

Simon Grayson, defender, 27. Regular full-back for the past six seasons. Can play on either flank and has adapted well to the wingback role favoured by manager Martin O'Neill. Has worn the captain's armband in the absence of Steve Walsh and became the semifinal hero with the goal at Wimbledon which saw City win on away goals.

Steve Walsh, defender, 32. Club captain and chief motivator who signed for Leicester from Wigan 11 years ago. Tough defender who has struggled through a series of injury problems this season. Will relish the task of keeping Ravanelli quiet and would love to lift the cup for the team he has taken to his heart.

Julian Watts, defender, 26. Former Sheffield Wednesday defender who has lost his place recently following the arrival of Matt Elliott. But with the new man cup-tied, Watts could step in and enjoy the biggest day out of his career to date.

Spencer Prior, defender, 25. Manager Martin O'Neill returned to his former club to capture Prior from Norwich for 1.2 million pounds ($2 million) earlier this season. Big and strong in the air he has become a central figure in Leicester's three-man backline.

Mike Whitlow, defender, 29. A regular last season, Whitlow has missed most of the current term through injury. Former Leeds United defender who just missed out on a championship medal in 1992 after failing to play enough games.
Pontus Kaamark, defender/midfielder, 28 on Saturday. Swedish international who has spent most of his career at Filbert Street on the treatment table after signing from IFK Gothenburg.

Neil Lennon, midfielder, 25. Northern Ireland midfielder who has been a key figure in Leicester's success this season. Good on the ball and a keen worker when not in possession. Has a fiery temper, but when he concentrates on threading passes into space for the frontmen he is one of the best in the top-flight.

Scott Taylor, midfielder, 26. Pacy player who is useful at putting pressure on opposing midfielders and making breaks to join in quickfire attacks. Injury and illness have stifled his progress, but his combative hard-running style have made him a fan's favourite. Signed from Reading for 500,000 pounds ($821,000) in July 1995.

Garry Parker, midfielder, 31. Worries over the health of his new-born baby daughter who was born prematurely could determine whether the much-travelled midfielder plays or not. When he does he plays an influential role in the middle for Leicester. Switches play cleverfully and uses deadball situations to deliver perfect crosses for the big men at the back.

Muzzy Izzet, midfielder, 22. Joined Leicester from Chelsea for 800,000 pounds ($1.3 million) after failing to get a chance to shine at Stamford Bridge. Hardworking midfielder who fits the bill to lead Leicester's pressing game. Will try to ensure Juninho and Co. are unable to enjoy time on the ball.

Emile Heskey, forward, 19. Outstanding prospect who is already scaring premier league defences with his strong running and eye for goal. Nicknamed "Bruno" after boxer Frank Bruno by the fans because of his strong physique. An England Under-21 regular and a star in the making.

Steve Claridge, forward, 30. Played for many years in the lower divisions and has done well in his first season in the top division. Will enjoy returning to Wembley after his last minute goal in the promotion play-off final against Palace earned Leicester promotion last season.

Mark Robins, forward, 27. Former Manchester United striker who moved to Leicester from Norwich two years ago. Rarely used by O'Neill until recently and nearly moved abroad following a trial period in Denmark with FC Copenhagen. Scored vital winner against Ipswich to ensure the City reached the semifinal. Likely to start on the sub's bench.
Jamie Lawrence, forward, 27. Former Doncaster attacker who has spent most of the season on the bench. Look for him to be flung into the action if O'Neill decides he needs more pace in his attacks.

Manager: Martin O'Neill. Age 45. Former Northern Ireland international who enjoyed great success with Nottingham Forest as a player and was in the side that won the European Cup in 1980. After managing at Wycombe and Norwich became Leicester manager in December 1995.
